language.notice.showing.description: Notice shown once after Homeroom picked the device's language automatically. {{language}} is that language's own name, for example Español.

language.notice.dismiss.description: Accessible label of the close button on the automatic-language notice.

language.notice.switchToEnglish.description: Button on the automatic-language notice. Always shown in English, whatever language is active, so a person who cannot read the picked language can find it.

tabs.sections.description: Accessible name of the main navigation: the tab bar on a phone, the left rail on a desktop.

tabs.home.description: Tab in the main navigation: opens the Home screen, the launcher of the person's apps.

tabs.discover.description: Tab in the main navigation on a computer's sidebar, and on a phone the name of the Discover page, which Home's Discover section opens: the screen for finding apps and communities to join.

tabs.ai.description: Tab in the main navigation: opens the person's page with Homeroom bot, the AI that builds what people ask for (their private chat with it and their work across projects). The bot's own name. On a phone it sits under an icon in a bar of five, in one of its two wider seats; keep it within about twelve characters.

tabs.unreadAi.text: Unread messages from the Homeroom bot
tabs.unreadAi.description: Spoken name of the small count on the AI tab in the main navigation: how many messages from the Homeroom bot the person has not read.

tabs.unreadAiTitle_one.text: {{count}} unread message from the Homeroom bot
tabs.unreadAiTitle_one.description: Tooltip on the count badge of the Homeroom bot tab in the main navigation: how many messages from the Homeroom bot the person has not read.

tabs.unreadAiTitle_other.text: {{count}} unread messages from the Homeroom bot
tabs.unreadAiTitle_other.description: Tooltip on the count badge of the Homeroom bot tab in the main navigation: how many messages from the Homeroom bot the person has not read.

tabs.messages.description: Tab in the main navigation: opens the person's conversations with people and agents.

tabs.communities.description: Tab in the main navigation: opens the communities the person belongs to. A community is a group that owns projects.

tabs.me.description: Last tab in the main navigation: opens the person's own profile, their account and settings. A short word for the person themselves, like "Me"; it must fit under an icon in a fifth of a phone's width.

tabs.meNamed.description: Accessible name of the profile tab when signed in. The tab shows only the word for You; this adds whose account it is. {{username}} is the person's username. Keep the word for You first.

tabs.communitiesOn.description: Accessible name of the Communities tab while it is showing one community. {{community}} is that community's name. Keep the word for Communities first.

tabs.communitiesVotes_one.description: Accessible name of the Communities tab on All communities while votes are waiting: the tab's word, then what its blue number counts. Keep the word for Communities first.

tabs.communitiesVotes_other.description: Accessible name of the Communities tab on All communities while votes are waiting: the tab's word, then what its blue number counts. Keep the word for Communities first.

tabs.communitiesOnVotes_one.text: Communities, on {{community}}, {{count}} vote waiting on you
tabs.communitiesOnVotes_one.description: Accessible name of the Communities tab while it is showing one community and votes are waiting there. {{community}} is that community's name; the count is its blue number. Keep the word for Communities first.

tabs.communitiesOnVotes_other.text: Communities, on {{community}}, {{count}} votes waiting on you
tabs.communitiesOnVotes_other.description: Accessible name of the Communities tab while it is showing one community and votes are waiting there. {{community}} is that community's name; the count is its blue number. Keep the word for Communities first.

tabs.votesWaiting_one.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the number badge on the Communities tab: how many proposals are waiting for this person's vote.

tabs.votesWaiting_other.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the number badge on the Communities tab: how many proposals are waiting for this person's vote.

tabs.unreadConversations.description: Accessible name of the number badge on the Messages tab. The number counts conversations with something unread, not messages.

tabs.unreadChannels.description: Accessible name of the number badge on the Communities tab. The number counts community channels that have unread messages.

tabs.stripApps.description: Small heading in the column of tabs down the side of an iPhone Duo's screen, over the app the person has open and the one they left: it divides those apps from the places above them (Home, Discover, Messages, Communities).

tabs.stripResume.description: Accessible name of the app the person left, in the Apps section of that side column: pressing it goes back into {{app}} as it was left. {{app}} is the app's name.

tabs.settings.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the cog at the foot of the desktop rail: opens Settings.

rail.communities.description: Heading over the desktop sidebar's list of communities: the ones pinned to its top, then the ones the viewer opened lately, each staying where it first arrived.

rail.search.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the small search button beside the Communities heading in the desktop sidebar: opens the list of all the person's communities with its search box ready to type in.

rail.all_one.description: Row under the person's communities in the desktop sidebar, opening the list of every community they are in, shown only when they are in more than the five the sidebar lists. {{count}} is how many there are (here 1).

rail.all_other.description: Row under the person's communities in the desktop sidebar, opening the list of every community they are in, shown only when they are in more than the five the sidebar lists. {{count}} is how many there are.

rail.allPlain.description: Row under the person's communities in the desktop sidebar, before their communities have loaded or when the sidebar already lists every one of them: opens the list of every community they are in.

rail.hideSidebar.description: Accessible name of the header button that folds the desktop navigation rail away, while the rail is showing.

rail.showSidebar.description: Accessible name of the header button that brings the desktop navigation rail back, while the rail is folded away.

rail.skipToNavigation.description: Link shown only to keyboard users at the top of the page: moves focus to the main navigation.

rail.pinned.description: Heading over the desktop sidebar's list of communities when some are pinned to its top; the same heading as the list under it.

rail.app.description: First row under a community in the desktop sidebar: opens the community's app, the thing its members build and use. Shown under the community's name, so it says only App.

rail.appOf.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the App row under a community in the desktop sidebar, which opens that community's app. {{name}} is the community's name.

rail.pin.here.description: The dashed slot the desktop sidebar draws under Pinned while an app's tile is dragged over from Pinned apps: dropping the tile there pins the app's community to the sidebar.

rail.pin.already.description: The same slot when the dragged app's community is pinned to the sidebar already: dropping it would change nothing, so the drop is refused.

rail.pin.full.description: The same slot when four communities are already pinned, the most there is room for: the drop is refused until one is taken off.

rail.pin.add.description: Item in the right-click menu of a community's row in the desktop sidebar or in All communities: keeps the community in the sidebar's Pinned section, above the person's other communities.

rail.pin.newTab.description: Item in the same right-click menu: opens the community's page in a new browser tab, as the browser's own menu for a link would.

rail.pin.fullToast.text: Four communities are pinned already. Unpin one first.
rail.pin.fullToast.description: Short message shown when the person tries to pin a fifth community to the desktop sidebar: four is the most there is room for.

rail.pin.unpin.description: The one item in the right-click menu of a community pinned to the desktop sidebar, and the caption on its tile while it is dragged out of the sidebar: it takes the community off the pinned list.

parked.resume.description: Label on the strip for an app the person left running: pressing the strip returns to that app as it was left.

parked.forget.description: Accessible name of the close button on the strip for an app left running: stops keeping {{app}} open. {{app}} is the app's name.

liveApp.stillOpen.description: Added to the accessible name of an app's row or tile, after the app's name, when the app is still loaded and will resume as it was left. One item in a list of facts.

liveApp.dotTitle.description: Tooltip of the small dot on an app that is still loaded and will resume as it was left.

liveApp.close.description: Accessible name of the button that closes an app still open in the background, on its App row in the desktop sidebar. {{app}} is the app's name, such as "Chess app".

liveApp.closeTitle.description: Tooltip of that same button, shown where the green still-open dot was.

header.back.description: Accessible name of the header's back button when it returns to the previous screen.

header.closeApp.description: Accessible name of the header's back button when it closes the app on screen and returns to Home.

header.home.description: Accessible name of the header's back button when it leads to the Home screen.

header.notifications.description: Accessible name of the bell button in the header: opens the list of notifications.

header.unreadNotifications.description: Accessible name of the number badge on the header's bell button.

header.communities.description: Title in the header on the screen that lists all of the person's communities.

header.switchCommunity.description: Accessible name of the header button on a community's page: opens the list for switching to another community. {{community}} is the current community's name; keep it first.

header.homeroomMenu.description: Accessible name of the Homeroom logo button in the header: opens the main menu. Homeroom is the product's name and is not translated.

header.changeBuilding.text: One of your changes is building
header.changeBuilding.description: Tooltip on the Homeroom logo button while a spinner shows on it: a change this person asked for is being built.

header.inApp.suggest.description: Small button in the header while an app is running: opens the form for suggesting an improvement to the app on screen.

header.inApp.suggestLabel.description: Accessible name of the header's Suggest button while an app is running: opens the form for suggesting an improvement to the app on screen.

chromeless.openAppLabel.description: Accessible name of the floating pill shown when an app is displayed without Homeroom's own header and tabs: opens the same app inside Homeroom.

chromeless.open.description: Text of the floating pill shown when an app is displayed without Homeroom's own header and tabs: opens the same app inside Homeroom.

banner.viewAsNonAdmin.text.description: Banner across the top for an administrator who chose to preview Homeroom as an ordinary member.

banner.viewAsNonAdmin.switchBack.description: Button in the banner for an administrator previewing as an ordinary member: returns to the administrator view.

banner.offline.text.text: Reconnecting to Homeroom. Showing saved content
banner.offline.text.description: Banner across the top while the device cannot reach Homeroom's servers and the screens show what was saved earlier. Homeroom is the product's name. No full stop at the end.

banner.restart.text.description: Banner across the top for a moment while Homeroom restarts for an update; the screen reconnects by itself. Homeroom is the product's name. No full stop at the end.

list.pair.description: How two independent facts are joined when an accessible name lists several, for example "App: Recipe Box, still open, unread". {{first}} is everything said so far and {{second}} the next fact. Only the punctuation between them is translated.

common.cancel.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: abandons the dialog or the action in progress and changes nothing.

common.close.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: closes the dialog, sheet or panel it is on. Also the accessible name of an X button that does this.

common.back.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: returns to the previous screen or step.

common.retry.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: repeats a request that failed.

common.tryAgain.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: repeats an action that failed.

common.save.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: saves the form it is on.

common.done.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: finishes and closes a dialog or an editing mode when there is nothing left to confirm.

common.ok.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: acknowledges a message and closes it.

common.copy.description: Generic button, used only where the control is exactly this and nothing about the place changes its meaning: copies the text or link beside it to the clipboard.

common.dismiss.description: Accessible name of an X button that hides a notice or banner without acting on it. Generic: used only where nothing about the place changes its meaning.

common.copied.description: Generic confirmation shown briefly in place of a Copy button after the text or link was copied to the clipboard.

common.loading.description: Generic placeholder shown while content is being fetched, where nothing more specific is said about what is loading.

ui.passwordInput.show.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the eye button inside a password field while the password is hidden as dots: pressing it shows the typed characters.

ui.passwordInput.hide.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the eye button inside a password field while the typed characters are visible: pressing it hides them as dots again.

ui.chat.newMessages.description: Accessible name of the line drawn across a chat transcript above the first message the reader has not seen yet. Read by screen readers only.

ui.chat.newLine.description: The one word shown at the end of the line that separates messages already read from unread ones in a chat transcript. An adjective: the messages below the line are new.

join.prompt.title.description: Title of the confirmation dialog shown when a person who is not a member tries to take part (vote, post, start a change) in a community's project. {{community}} is the project or community's name. Join is a verb: become a member.

join.prompt.message.text: Members start changes, file requests, vote and chat here. Join to take part.
join.prompt.message.description: Body of the join confirmation dialog, under its title: says what members of the community can do and that joining is needed to do it. Requests are requests for a change to the project; Join is a verb.

join.prompt.join.description: Confirm button of the join confirmation dialog: makes the person a member of the community named in the title, then repeats what they were trying to do. Verb.

join.prompt.notNow.description: Cancel button of the join confirmation dialog: closes it without joining the community.

time.ago.justNow.description: Age of an item (a message, card or notification) that is less than a minute old, shown as a small stamp on its row. Lower case because it sits in the middle of a line.

time.ago.minutes_one.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} minute old. 'm' abbreviates minute; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.ago.minutes_other.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} minutes old (under an hour). 'm' abbreviates minutes; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.ago.hours_one.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} hour old. 'h' abbreviates hour; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.ago.hours_other.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} hours old (under a day). 'h' abbreviates hours; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.ago.days_one.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} day old. 'd' abbreviates day; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.ago.days_other.description: Compact age stamp on a card, list or notification row for something {{count}} days old (under a week). 'd' abbreviates days; keep it as short as the language allows.

time.reset.weekly.description: When a weekly allowance comes back, in the reader's own time zone. Used only to replace the words "Monday 00:00 UTC" inside a sentence the server wrote in English (for example "Weekly limit reached. Resets Monday 00:00 UTC."), so it must read as the end of an English sentence after "Resets". Homeroom's own sentences about a reset are whole entries elsewhere. {{day}} is the weekday's full name and {{time}} the time of day.

time.reset.daily.description: When a daily allowance comes back, in the reader's own time zone. Used only to replace the words "at midnight UTC" inside a sentence the server wrote in English, so it must read as the end of an English sentence after "Resets" or "They reset". Homeroom's own sentences about a reset are whole entries elsewhere. {{time}} is the time of day.

spec.screens.afterLabel.description: Accessible name of the 'after' picture in a proposal's before/after screens: the screen as it is planned to look. {{changes}} is the author's own description of what changes on that screen.

spec.screens.beforeLabel.description: Accessible name of the 'before' picture in a proposal's before/after screens: the screen as it looks today. {{changes}} is the author's own description of what changes on that screen.

spec.screens.afterChip.description: Small chip over the 'after' picture in a proposal's before/after screens: this side shows the planned look, not something built yet. Keep the middle dot.

spec.screens.beforeChip.description: Small chip over the 'before' picture in a proposal's before/after screens: this side shows how the screen looks today. Keep the middle dot.

spec.screens.metaPhone.description: Caption under a proposal's before/after screen drawn at phone size. {{width}} and {{height}} are the screen's size in pixels; {{persona}} is the kind of viewer the screen is shown for, in the author's own word (member, admin). Keep the multiplication sign and the middle dot.

spec.screens.metaDesktop.description: Caption under a proposal's before/after screen drawn at desktop size. {{width}} and {{height}} are the screen's size in pixels; {{persona}} is the kind of viewer the screen is shown for, in the author's own word (member, admin). Keep the multiplication sign and the middle dot.

spec.screens.metaPhoneZoom.text: Phone, {{width}} × {{height}}<0> · close-up</0><1> · whole screen</1> · seen as a {{persona}}
spec.screens.metaPhoneZoom.description: Caption under a proposal's before/after screen drawn at phone size, when the picture can switch between a close-up of the changed part and the whole screen. Only one of the two tagged parts is visible at a time: <0> while the close-up is shown, <1> while the whole screen is shown, so the line must read correctly with either one alone. {{width}} and {{height}} are the size in pixels; {{persona}} is the kind of viewer, in the author's own word (member, admin).

spec.screens.metaDesktopZoom.text: Desktop, {{width}} × {{height}}<0> · close-up</0><1> · whole screen</1> · seen as a {{persona}}
spec.screens.metaDesktopZoom.description: Caption under a proposal's before/after screen drawn at desktop size, when the picture can switch between a close-up of the changed part and the whole screen. Only one of the two tagged parts is visible at a time: <0> while the close-up is shown, <1> while the whole screen is shown, so the line must read correctly with either one alone. {{width}} and {{height}} are the size in pixels; {{persona}} is the kind of viewer, in the author's own word (member, admin).

ui.chat.replies_one.description: Label of the control under a chat message that opens its thread of replies, when the thread has {{count}} reply. Reply is a noun here: a message written in answer.

ui.chat.replies_other.description: Label of the control under a chat message that opens its thread of replies. {{count}} is how many replies the thread has. Replies is a noun here: messages written in answer.

ui.cardRun.more_one.description: Row in a chat transcript that stands for cards folded away after the first of a run of cards in a row (proposals, shared items); pressing it shows them. {{count}} is how many are hidden, here one. Keep the leading ellipsis.

ui.cardRun.more_other.description: Row in a chat transcript that stands for cards folded away after the first of a run of cards in a row (proposals, shared items); pressing it shows them. {{count}} is how many are hidden. Keep the leading ellipsis.

illustration.error.type.text: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP under 20 MB.
illustration.error.type.description: Error under the picture chooser of an illustration editor (an app's featured illustration, a challenge's artwork) when the chosen file is not one of these image formats or is larger than 20 megabytes. PNG, JPEG and WebP are file format names.

illustration.error.unreadable.text: That image could not be read. Choose another image.
illustration.error.unreadable.description: Error under the picture chooser of an illustration editor when the browser could not open the chosen image file, for example because it is damaged.

illustration.error.noSize.text: Choose an image with a valid size.
illustration.error.noSize.description: Error under the picture chooser of an illustration editor when the chosen image reports no width or height, so it cannot be drawn.

illustration.error.noCanvas.text: Image editing is unavailable in this browser.
illustration.error.noCanvas.description: Error under the picture chooser of an illustration editor when the browser cannot resize images, so the chosen picture cannot be prepared for upload.

illustration.error.tooLarge.description: Error under the picture chooser of an illustration editor when the chosen picture is still over the upload limit after it was shrunk. Smaller means fewer pixels or a smaller file.

release.sentence.waiting.description: Says when a change merged into Homeroom itself goes live, on every surface that shows such a change (a change's page, a card's tooltip, a chat card): it was merged but Homeroom's next release is held up, so no time is promised. No full stop: the surrounding message adds it.

release.sentence.now.description: Says when a change merged into Homeroom itself goes live, on every surface that shows such a change (a change's page, a card's tooltip, a chat card): the Homeroom release that carries it is rolling out now. No full stop: the surrounding message adds it.

release.sentence.next.text: Merged; goes live in the next release
release.sentence.next.description: Says when a change merged into Homeroom itself goes live, on every surface that shows such a change (a change's page, a card's tooltip, a chat card): it goes out with Homeroom's next release, and no time is known yet. No full stop: the surrounding message adds it.

release.sentence.minutes_one.text: Merged; goes live in the next release (in about a minute)
release.sentence.minutes_one.description: Says when a change merged into Homeroom itself goes live, on every surface that shows such a change (a change's page, a card's tooltip, a chat card): it goes out with Homeroom's next release, expected in about {{count}} minute. English spells the one minute out; a translation may use {{count}}. No full stop: the surrounding message adds it.

release.sentence.minutes_other.text: Merged; goes live in the next release (about {{count}} minutes)
release.sentence.minutes_other.description: Says when a change merged into Homeroom itself goes live, on every surface that shows such a change (a change's page, a card's tooltip, a chat card): it goes out with Homeroom's next release, expected in about {{count}} minutes. No full stop: the surrounding message adds it.

release.short.waiting.description: Short status of a change merged into Homeroom itself, on a line that already says it merged (a list row's second line, a status line): Homeroom's next release is held up, so no time is promised.

release.short.now.description: Short status of a change merged into Homeroom itself, on a line that already says it merged (a list row's second line, a status line): the Homeroom release that carries it is rolling out now.

release.short.next.text: Goes live in the next release
release.short.next.description: Short status of a change merged into Homeroom itself, on a line that already says it merged (a list row's second line, a status line): it goes out with Homeroom's next release, and no time is known yet.

release.short.minutes_one.text: Goes live in about a minute
release.short.minutes_one.description: Short status of a change merged into Homeroom itself, on a line that already says it merged (a list row's second line, a status line): Homeroom's next release, which carries it, is expected in about {{count}} minute. English spells the one minute out; a translation may use {{count}}.

release.short.minutes_other.description: Short status of a change merged into Homeroom itself, on a line that already says it merged (a list row's second line, a status line): Homeroom's next release, which carries it, is expected in about {{count}} minutes.

release.countLine.waiting_one.text: {{count}} merged change waiting for a release
release.countLine.waiting_one.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} change (here 1) was merged and Homeroom's next release, which would carry it, is held up.

release.countLine.waiting_other.text: {{count}} merged changes waiting for a release
release.countLine.waiting_other.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} changes were merged and Homeroom's next release, which would carry them, is held up.

release.countLine.now_one.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged change (here 1) is going live now, as the Homeroom release that carries it rolls out.

release.countLine.now_other.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged changes are going live now, as the Homeroom release that carries them rolls out.

release.countLine.next_one.text: {{count}} merged change goes live in the next release
release.countLine.next_one.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged change (here 1) goes out with Homeroom's next release, and no time is known yet.

release.countLine.next_other.text: {{count}} merged changes go live in the next release
release.countLine.next_other.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged changes go out together with Homeroom's next release, and no time is known yet.

release.countLine.estimate_one.text: {{count}} merged change goes live in the next release ({{eta}})
release.countLine.estimate_one.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged change (here 1) goes out with Homeroom's next release. {{eta}} is when that release is expected, worded on its own, for example "about 8 minutes" or "in about a minute".

release.countLine.estimate_other.text: {{count}} merged changes go live in the next release ({{eta}})
release.countLine.estimate_other.description: Status line at the top of Homeroom's own Workshop board "Done" column: {{count}} merged changes go out together with Homeroom's next release. {{eta}} is when that release is expected, worded on its own, for example "about 8 minutes" or "in about a minute".

release.countLine.eta_one.description: When Homeroom's next release is expected, placed in brackets after "… merged changes go live in the next release" on the Workshop board's "Done" column: in about {{count}} minute. English spells the one minute out; a translation may use {{count}}. Lower case because it sits inside that line.

release.countLine.eta_other.description: When Homeroom's next release is expected, placed in brackets after "… merged changes go live in the next release" on the Workshop board's "Done" column: in about {{count}} minutes. Lower case because it sits inside that line.

sectionColumn.label.description: Accessible name of the column beside a project's page on a wide screen that lists its places (its chat, its topics and its tabs).

dictation.speak.description: Microphone button: records speech to add to the current text field.

dictation.stop.description: Button: finishes the recording and transcribes it into the text field.

dictation.permission.description: Status while the browser microphone permission prompt is open.

dictation.transcribing.description: Status while a finished recording is being transcribed.

dictation.cancel.description: Button: discards the recording or pending transcription and keeps existing text.

dictation.listening.text: Listening… Press Stop when you finish.
dictation.listening.description: Status while recording speech, with instructions for finishing.

dictation.error.permission.text: Allow microphone access in your browser or device settings, then try again.
dictation.error.permission.description: Dictation error when microphone access was denied.

dictation.error.policy.text: Microphone access is blocked on this page. You can still type your message.
dictation.error.policy.description: Dictation error when the page's permissions policy prevents microphone access. Browser microphone settings cannot override this restriction.

dictation.error.unsupported.text: Speaking is unavailable in this browser. You can still type your message.
dictation.error.unsupported.description: Dictation error when recording is unsupported.

dictation.error.unavailable.text: Your microphone could not start. Check that it is connected, then try again.
dictation.error.unavailable.description: Dictation error when a microphone cannot be opened.

dictation.error.interrupted.text: Recording stopped unexpectedly. Your existing text is safe. Try again.
dictation.error.interrupted.description: Dictation error when microphone capture is interrupted.

dictation.error.invalidAudio.text: That recording could not be read. Try a recording under one minute.
dictation.error.invalidAudio.description: Dictation error for invalid or over-limit audio.

dictation.error.noSpeech.text: No speech was heard. Try again and speak closer to the microphone.
dictation.error.noSpeech.description: Dictation error when the recording was silent or had no transcript.

dictation.error.keyRequired.text: Your AI connection is unavailable. Check AI usage & models in Settings, then try again.
dictation.error.keyRequired.description: Dictation error when the account’s managed or personal AI credential is unavailable.

dictation.error.credits.text: Your AI credits have run out. Add credits in Settings, then try again.
dictation.error.credits.description: Dictation error when the transcription provider reports exhausted credits.

dictation.error.tooLong.text: Those words would exceed this field’s limit. Shorten your text and try again.
dictation.error.tooLong.description: Dictation error when appending the transcript would exceed the current field character limit.

dictation.error.timeout.text: Transcription took too long. Your existing text is safe. Try again.
dictation.error.timeout.description: Dictation error after a transcription timeout.

dictation.error.busy.text: Please wait a moment before recording again.
dictation.error.busy.description: Dictation error for concurrent requests or a rate limit.

dictation.error.failed.text: Your recording could not be transcribed. Your existing text is safe. Try again.
dictation.error.failed.description: Dictation error for an unsuccessful transcription request.

header.drawer.toHub.description: On a phone, the header's back arrow on one of a community's places (Needs you, Workshop, a channel): goes up to the community's Hub, the page that leads to all of them. {{community}} is the community's name. Its accessible name and tooltip.

header.drawer.toPlace.description: On a phone, the header's back arrow on a page under one of a community's places (All items, under the Workshop): goes up to that place. {{place}} is the place's name, such as Workshop. Its accessible name and tooltip.

header.drawer.toBot.description: On a phone, the header's back arrow in Main Chat, the person's private chat with Homeroom bot: slides back to the Homeroom bot tab's list of what needs them and what is in progress. Its accessible name and tooltip.

header.drawer.messages.description: On a phone, the header's title over the list of the person's conversations, when the conversations are drawn as the navigation drawer's outer level.

header.drawer.toMessages.description: On a phone, the header's back arrow in a conversation: slides back to the list of the person's conversations.

work.stage.reading.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: Homeroom bot, the platform's builder bot, is reading the request, or it waits to be read.

work.stage.notStarted.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: nobody has started on the request yet: it waits in Homeroom bot's line, or for anyone to pick it up.

work.stage.readyToBuild.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: Homeroom bot read it and will build it, but it waits its turn among the project's builds.

work.stage.planning.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: Homeroom bot is writing its plan for the request.

work.stage.waitingForYou.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: it is the requester's move (shown to them).

work.stage.building.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: the change for it is being built.

work.stage.checking.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: its change's tests are running, or some failed.

work.stage.syncing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: its change conflicts with main and Homeroom is resolving that now or next, with nobody asked for anything.

work.stage.upForVote.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: its change is waiting for the group's votes.

work.stage.goingLive.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: its change was approved and is being put live.

work.stage.live.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: its change is live.

work.stage.stopped.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: Homeroom bot stopped working on it; a person can start it again.

work.stage.closed.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The stage word: the request or the change was closed.

work.why.question.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to the requester: Homeroom bot asked them a question and waits for the answer.

work.why.plan.text: Waiting for you to OK the plan
work.why.plan.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to the requester: Homeroom bot wrote a plan and waits for them to say build it.

work.why.decide.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to the requester: Homeroom bot handed it back because a person must decide what to do.

work.why.alreadyWorks.text: It may already work: close it?
work.why.alreadyWorks.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to the requester: Homeroom bot found that what was asked for is already there, so it can be closed.

work.why.needsDetail.text: Waiting for more detail from you
work.why.needsDetail.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to the requester: Homeroom bot could not tell what to build and needs more detail.

work.whyOthers.question.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to someone other than the requester: Homeroom bot asked the requester a question.

work.whyOthers.plan.text: Waiting for the plan to be OK'd
work.whyOthers.plan.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to someone other than the requester: Homeroom bot's plan waits for the requester's go-ahead.

work.whyOthers.decide.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to someone other than the requester: a person must decide what to do with it.

work.whyOthers.alreadyWorks.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to someone other than the requester: Homeroom bot found what was asked for already there.

work.whyOthers.needsDetail.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Shown to someone other than the requester: Homeroom bot needs more detail to build it.

work.reason.buildFailed.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Homeroom bot's build of it did not finish.

work.reason.fixStopped.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Homeroom bot stopped fixing its change's failing tests, at its own limit.

work.reason.lookFailed.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Homeroom bot's read of the request failed.

work.reason.changeClosed.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). the change made for the request was closed while the request is still open.

work.reason.stalled.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). the build was queued but never started.

work.line.queued.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: it waits in Homeroom bot's line on its project.

work.line.firstVersionWait.text: Waiting for the first version to go live
work.line.firstVersionWait.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). The second line under Not started yet: the request was filed while its project's first version is not live yet, and Homeroom bot starts on it as soon as that version goes live.

work.line.queuedAt.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: its place in Homeroom bot's line on its project. {{place}} is a number, 1 for next.

work.line.heldBuilds.text: Waiting for one of the project's builds to finish
work.line.heldBuilds.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: ready to build, but the project's builds are all under way.

work.line.heldWaiting.text: Waiting for changes up for a vote to be decided
work.line.heldWaiting.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: ready to build, but the project's changes waiting for votes hold its slots.

work.line.onHold.text: On hold until Monday: this week's building time is used up
work.line.onHold.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the project's building time for the week is used up.

work.line.cooldown.text: Paused after repeated errors: Homeroom bot tries again later
work.line.cooldown.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: Homeroom bot's tries at reading the request failed several times in a row, so it waits a day before trying again. Nothing to do with building time.

work.line.reply.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: Homeroom bot is reading what the person replied.

work.line.retryPlan.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the plan could not be written, and Homeroom bot is trying again.

work.line.reviewing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: Homeroom bot reviews its own change before putting it up. {{round}} and {{of}} are numbers.

work.line.starting.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the build is starting.

work.line.proposing.text: Putting it up for a vote
work.line.proposing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the change is being put up for the group's vote.

work.line.fixing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: Homeroom bot is fixing its change's failing tests.

work.line.revising.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the change is being updated with what was asked for.

work.line.updateQueued.text: An update is on its way
work.line.updateQueued.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: an update to the change waits its turn, so the vote waits for it.

work.line.checksFailing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: some of its change's tests failed.

work.line.checksFailingCount_one.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: how many of its change's tests failed. {{count}} is a number.

work.line.checksFailingCount_other.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: how many of its change's tests failed. {{count}} is a number.

work.line.checksRunning_one.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Checking: about how long its tests have left, from the same estimate its Testing card shows. {{count}} is a number of minutes, at least 1.

work.line.checksRunning_other.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Checking: about how long its tests have left, from the same estimate its Testing card shows. {{count}} is a number of minutes, at least 1.

work.line.syncWait.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Checking: the change conflicts with main, so its tests wait until it is synced, and nobody is asked to vote on it yet.

work.line.conflictOnYes.text: Conflicts with main: Homeroom resolves it once you approve
work.line.conflictOnYes.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line of a change up for a vote that conflicts with main: a yes lets Homeroom resolve the conflict, re-run the checks and merge it without asking again.

work.line.githubChecks.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Going live: the change has the yes it needs, and GitHub has not merged it yet because the required checks GitHub runs on it are still running, or failed and are being run again on today's main. Homeroom merges it once they pass.

work.line.githubChecksFailing.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Checking: the change has the yes it needs, but the required checks GitHub runs on it failed again after Homeroom brought it up to date with main, so its author (or Homeroom bot, for its own change) has to fix them before it can merge.

work.line.githubWait.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line under Going live: the change has the yes it needs, and GitHub held its merge back for a moment (busy, or a refusal nobody has to act on). Homeroom tries again in a few minutes.

work.line.firstVersion.text: First version: it goes live without a vote
work.line.firstVersion.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: a project's first version is put live once its tests pass, with no vote.

work.line.claimed.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: a person pressed Claim on the request. {{username}} is their username.

work.line.planningWithYou.text: Planning it with you in a private thread
work.line.planningWithYou.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: the requester is shaping the plan with Homeroom bot in a thread of their own.

work.line.waiting.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: nobody has started on it yet.

work.line.said.description: Where a request or a change stands, the same words on every screen (the Homeroom bot tab, the chat's drawer, a request's page, a project's chat, the bell). Second line: Homeroom bot's own one-line reason. {{reason}} is its sentence, already in the person's language or English.

rail.pin.keepTop.text: Keep {{name}} at the top of Recents
rail.pin.keepTop.description: Accessible name of the pin button on a row of the desktop sidebar's Recents. {{name}} is the community's name.

rail.pin.unpinTop.text: Unpin {{name}} from the top of Recents
rail.pin.unpinTop.description: Accessible name of the pin button on a pinned row of the desktop sidebar's Recents. {{name}} is the community's name.

header.drawer.toHome.description: Accessible name of the back button in the header on a community's Hub on a phone: returns to Home, where the viewer's communities are.
